title: Keeping Up with Science: We Are Living in the Most Creative Time Ever

elements.content: Master the core scientific vocabulary and collocations for this topic (10 items):

items.definition: the action of making something accessible to everyone.
items.example: The digitization of music recording software led to the democratization of music production.

items.definition: a very large quantity of something.
items.example: We have an abundance of high-quality learning content available for free online.

items.definition: a process followed by a computer to filter or recommend content.
items.example: Social media algorithms decide which creative works get millions of views.

items.definition: the action of earning revenue from an asset or online content.
items.example: Platform monetization allows creators to quit their day jobs and focus on art.

items.definition: the state that occurs when no more of something can be absorbed or added.
items.example: The market is facing high saturation with thousands of new podcasts launched daily.

items.definition: concerned with beauty or the appreciation of physical beauty.
items.example: The app's minimalist aesthetic appeals to a very young and design-conscious audience.

items.definition: the process of selecting and organizing content.
items.example: Good curation is becoming more valuable than creating new content.

items.definition: a person or organization that controls who gets opportunities.
items.example: Before social media, publishers acted as cultural gatekeepers.

items.definition: relating to interests that appeal to a small, specialized audience.
items.example: The internet allows creators to build sustainable businesses around highly niche topics.

items.definition: skill in a particular craft; high-quality manual or artistic work.
items.example: Many worry that automatic digital filters destroy the need for genuine craftsmanship.

elements.title: Grammar Explanation (Advanced (C1))
elements.content:
Double comparatives (the more..., the more...) describe a parallel relationship where one change directly causes another.
🧩 Interactive Word Bank:
Tap a word chip below, then tap any empty bracket [_____] to place it!

greater
more connected
more open
harder
comparative

elements.text: Researchers conducted in-depth investigations and empirical trials to analyze these phenomena. The findings reveal critical mechanisms that challenge earlier assumptions.
elements.takeaway: Understanding both biological and empirical evidence allows us to draw more grounded conclusions.
